description: Apparatus surface after issue #570 (owner decision 2026-10-08: every tool call the server does not support is an error, without exception). Every input schema gains "additionalProperties": false, and the server refuses at call time, before the tool body runs, any call its listed schema does not admit: an unknown tool, an undeclared argument (named, with the tool's accepted arguments and, for a time-axis name such as observed_at, the tools that serve that axis), a wrong JSON type (strict: "5" is not an integer, 1 is not a boolean, the string "null" is not JSON null), a null where none is allowed, or a missing required argument (lovspor.mcp_contract.ContractServer). No tool name, description or output schema changes (eighteen tools), and every supported call answers byte-identically (pinned by tests/unit/test_mcp_existing_calls.py and, per tool, by tests/unit/test_mcp_call_contract.py). Supersedes tool-surface-v8.json for FUTURE runs; v1-v8 stay committed untouched because the runs that recorded their hashes must remain verifiable (pass --surface-path for a re-check against any of them). The call-time refusal is also a behaviour change the hash cannot see: a run that spans it would compare a lax server with a strict one, so take it between runs. The surface is corpus-independent (the schemas come from build_server, not the documents) but interpreter-dependent: tool descriptions come from docstrings, and CPython 3.13 dedents docstrings at compile time, so the hash is only defined together with the `python` field below. A unit test regenerates this document from the code on every run — names on every interpreter, hash on the apparatus interpreter; if the served surface changes, that test fails and changing this file is an explicit apparatus decision, not drift. check_fairness.py reads this document as the expectation the declared tool_config is compared against.
